name: Is a linear drain better than a center drain for a curbless shower?

mainEntity.name: Is a linear drain better than a center drain for a curbless shower?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A linear drain is not automatically better than a center drain; it is better only when it fits the room’s slope, tile, maintenance, and design requirements. Linear drains can place the slope in one direction, while center drains typically require the floor to slope from multiple sides.

The best choice depends on the shower dimensions, entry location, wall alignment, tile format, plumbing position, and budget. Elite Remodeling & Design can include drain selection within the larger bathroom design rather than choosing it after the floor layout is fixed.

Key factors:
- Linear drains may support larger tile in some layouts, but they require careful length and placement decisions.
- Center drains can be practical when existing plumbing and room geometry support them.
- Drain access, hair collection, finish, and replacement parts matter after installation.

Ask for the drain model, location, grate finish, cleaning method, and access plan in writing. Compare the complete installed cost, not just the drain component.

The right drain is the one that supports reliable slope and serviceability within the existing bathroom.
acceptedAnswer.description: Neither is universally better. A linear drain may simplify a one-direction slope, while a center drain can suit existing plumbing and compact layouts. Compare slope, tile format, cleaning access, appearance, plumbing work, and total installed cost.
